episode.title: HPR4747: UNIX Curio #13 - Replacements for cat
episode.author: Vance
episode.summary:
This series is dedicated to exploring little-known—and occasionally useful—trinkets lurking in the dusty corners of UNIX-like operating systems.

HPR episode 4657

chapters.title: Close but Not Perfect: sed and grep

quotes.text: None of the standard utilities are able to fully duplicate its functionality on their own. Some of them come close but can't quite be relied on in all respects.
I was hoping that a simple invocation of one of the standard utilities could be used in place of the CAT program that our prankster has deleted.

There are certainly other widespread tools, such as Perl, that could also be used in place of CAD. However, I wanted to focus only on utilities that are so ubiquitous that they appear in the POSIX standard.

notes.summary: This episode explores standard UNIX utilities that can partially or fully replace the 'cat' command for reading and outputting files. The host tests various tools like 'comm', 'tr', 'dd', 'awk', and others against POSIX standards, concluding that no single standard utility perfectly replicates 'cat' without limitations. Listeners interested in UNIX internals, POSIX compliance, and creative uses of command-line tools will find this detailed analysis informative.
